sources.title: Site Moves and Migrations - Google Search Central
verifiedClaims: Google recommends mapping old URLs to corresponding new URLs and preparing the redirect strategy from that map.
Google advises redirecting to the final destination directly when possible; chains add latency and some user agents may not support long chains.
Google recommends updating internal links, self-referencing canonical annotations, and the sitemap for the new URLs, and testing redirects after changes.

sources.title: Redirects and Google Search - Google Search Central
verifiedClaims: Google distinguishes permanent and temporary redirects and recommends permanent server-side redirects when a page has moved permanently and that behavior is appropriate.
Google identifies URL Inspection and command line or script checks as options for testing redirect behavior.

limitations: No ranking or traffic increase is promised.
The article asks a site administrator to confirm implementation because redirect setup varies by hosting and site environment.
The article separates chains, loops, not-found results, and irrelevant destinations rather than treating them as one defect.
